newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - quiet ahead of U.S. holiday.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - quiet ahead of U.S. holiday.

text.p: The New York physical coffee market was thinly traded this week ahead of the U.S. Labor Day holiday.
"It is very slow, there was only some intermittent spot business," one dealer said. "People are holding off until after the holiday."

Also putting a damper on activity was concern about the cost of carrying spot beans. With CSCE September holding an 10-cent premium to December ahead of its expiry, few buyers were willing to take coffee priced off the spot contract.
"The roasters can't see the wisdom of paying such a high premium for the spot," another dealer said.
CSCE spot contract's premium to the deferreds surged as concern grew about a shortage of coffee available for delivery against September.

Certified U.S. coffee stocks rose 4,797 bags on the week, to 39,313, the CSCE reported after the close of trading Monday. But spot September's open interest was still relatively high at 1,279 lots Thursday, the equivalent of about 320,000 bags of coffee.
